what: Cardan velocity ripple and differential subtraction. This 300-piece correctly phased Cardan control uses two equal bends, a symmetric differential and a pointer. The second joint cancels the first joint's periodic speed variation at the outer shaft. The mechanism displays angular motion; it does not transmit an elastic wave. Correct phasing cancels the outer-shaft ripple; compare the same one-motor program with WaveMaker. 298 placements plus two inferred crosses: 300 physical pieces.
try: Choose WaveMaker Control; its Blocks program loads automatically. Reset to the saved starting pose and press Run. The one-motor program runs four cycles at 30°/s, four at 60°/s, reverses through eight cycles, and then holds.
Reset and load WaveMaker to compare. Only the two downstream fork orientations change. The main pointer rocks while this control stays close to its initial angle.
Compare the reference shaft and output shaft. Correct phasing preserves the one-to-one outer-shaft relationship even though the intermediate shaft of the first joint has nonuniform speed.
why: For equal Cardan bends, correctly aligned middle forks make the second joint apply the inverse of the first joint's angle mapping. The outer shafts therefore have a constant one-to-one ideal ratio. The symmetric differential and 16:8 pointer takeoff show the remaining small numerical residual in the simulation.
matters: A correctly phased double Cardan can cancel the angular-speed variation produced by one bent universal joint. This is why alignment matters even when both arrangements have the same average ratio.
question: Why does the intermediate shaft speed up and slow down while the control pointer barely moves?
answer: One bent Cardan joint has a varying instantaneous ratio. The equal, correctly phased second joint reverses that variation at the outer output. The output stays at a one-to-one ideal angle ratio even though the intermediate shaft is not uniform.
further: The 48–64–80 shaft-center triangle gives β≈36.87°. For the correctly phased pair, the ideal outer-shaft relation is output angle = input angle; the measured pointer span is about 0.0164° over the complete run.
The model has 298 explicit placements plus two required inferred universal-joint crosses, for 300 pieces. It has one motor on port A and passive output shafts.
The automatic Blocks program uses 30 and 60 degrees per second, includes reversal and guarded holds, and should be run from the saved starting pose after Reset.
This is simulation evidence only. It does not establish physical buildability, torque capacity, friction, backlash, real-world swept clearance, or firmware behavior.
formula: For one Cardan joint, tan φ=tan θ/cos β. For equal bends with aligned middle forks the second joint is the inverse mapping, so outer output angle θout=θin and the ideal output speed ratio is 1.
